questions.stem: A can complete a piece of work in 10 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days. If they work together, in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.explanation: B is correct. A's rate = 1/10, B's rate = 1/15 per day. Together: 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6. Together they complete the work in 6 days. **Short Trick:** Combined days = (a×b)/(a+b) = (10×15)/(10+15) = 150/25 = 6 days.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 12 days. He works for 4 days, then stops. What fraction of the work is still remaining?
questions.explanation: D is correct. A's rate = 1/12 per day. In 4 days he completes 4/12 = 1/3 of the work. Remaining = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3 of the work.

questions.stem: 10 workers can complete a task in 6 days. How many days will 12 workers take to finish the same task?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Workers × Days = Total work units. 10 × 6 = 60 work-units. For 12 workers: 12 × D = 60 → D = 5 days. Inverse relation: more workers → fewer days.

questions.stem: A and B together can complete a job in 8 days. A alone takes 12 days. How many days will B take to finish the job alone?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Together rate = 1/8. A's rate = 1/12. B's rate = 1/8 − 1/12 = 3/24 − 2/24 = 1/24. B alone takes 24 days. **Short Trick:** B = (A×T)/(A−T) = (12×8)/(12−8) = 96/4 = 24 days.

questions.stem: A can do a piece of work in 20 days and B in 30 days. They start together. After 6 days, A leaves. How many more days will B need to finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Together: 1/20+1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12 per day. In 6 days: 6/12 = 1/2 done. Remaining = 1/2. B alone (1/30 per day): time = (1/2)÷(1/30) = 15 days.

questions.stem: 8 men can complete a job in 10 days. 10 women can complete the same job in 8 days. If 4 men and 5 women work together, how many days will they take to finish?
questions.explanation: B is correct. 1 man/day = 1/(8×10) = 1/80 work. 1 woman/day = 1/(10×8) = 1/80 work. Equal productivity per person! 4 men + 5 women = 9 people at 1/80 each = 9/80 per day. Days = 80/9 = 8 8/9 days.

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 8 hours and Pipe B can empty it in 12 hours. If both pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Net filling rate = 1/8 − 1/12 = 3/24 − 2/24 = 1/24 per hour. Tank fills in 24 hours. Note: when an inlet and an outlet are both open, subtract the empty rate from the fill rate.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes fill a tank in 20 and 30 minutes respectively. A drain empties it in 15 minutes. All three are opened simultaneously. In how many minutes will the tank fill?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Net fill rate = 1/20 + 1/30 − 1/15 = 3/60 + 2/60 − 4/60 = 1/60 per minute. Tank fills in 60 minutes. Note: sum of inlets = 5/60 = 1/12; minus drain 1/15 = 4/60. Net = 1/60.

questions.stem: A alone can do a work in X days and B alone in (X + 5) days. Together they finish in 6 days. Find X.
questions.explanation: B is correct. 1/X + 1/(X+5) = 1/6. (2X+5)/[X(X+5)] = 1/6 → 6(2X+5) = X(X+5) → 12X+30 = X²+5X → X²−7X−30 = 0 → (X−10)(X+3) = 0. X=10 (discarding negative). A takes 10 days, B takes 15 days. Check: 1/10+1/15 = 5/30 = 1/6 ✓.

questions.stem: A is twice as efficient as B. Together they can finish a piece of work in 18 days. How many days would A take to complete the work alone?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Let B take x days → A takes x/2 days (twice as efficient). Together: 1/(x/2) + 1/x = 2/x + 1/x = 3/x = 1/18 → x = 54 (B's time). A takes 54/2 = 27 days. Check: 1/27 + 1/54 = 2/54 + 1/54 = 3/54 = 1/18 ✓.
